title: Restoring the split-body configuration
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $a$ be one of its states, and let $w,s$ be Boolean words. Starting from the constructed restore-scan configuration indexed by zero, the split-body machine reaches the seam configuration with restore state $(4,\mathrm{false})$ and the updated tape word obtained by appending $1$ to $s$ when $|s|\\le |w|$, and otherwise leaving $s$ unchanged, after some $t\\le 2|s|+|w|+5$ steps. Throughout these steps it avoids its anchor state.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Boolean symbols
caveat: The conclusion uses private restore-scan, split-body, and seam-configuration constructions; their supplied informal descriptions are placeholders, preventing a fully self-contained account of those constructions.
